userStories.title: cam journal append end-to-end (tracer bullet)
userStories.description: As the read-only orchestrator, I need a deterministic `cam journal append` command that reads a structured JSON cycle entry on stdin, renders the canonical journal markdown block, and commits it to scripts/cam/journal.md on main via commit-tree, so that I can record a cycle without a Write or an ad-hoc jq-redirect.
acceptanceCriteria: cam journal append reads a structured JSON object on stdin (cycleId, started, closed, branch, issue, outcome, summary) and renders the canonical journal block (a `## <cycleId> — <title>` header line plus the bullet fields Started/Closed/Branch/Issue/Outcome/Summary) appended after the existing journal entries. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts]

The entry is committed to main via commit-tree (temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree main, hash-object -w --stdin, update-index --add --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree -p main, update-ref refs/heads/main), never touching the current work branch; the checked-out branch and HEAD are unchanged and the working tree stays clean. [oracle: real-git integration test in test/integration/journal-append-on-main.test.ts asserting `git rev-parse main` advanced by exactly one commit and `git rev-parse HEAD` on the feature branch plus `git status --porcelain` are unchanged]

The current journal.md is read from main via `git show main:scripts/cam/journal.md` (read-from-main, CAM-86 US-006 pattern), never from the working tree. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'main:scripts/cam/journal.md' src/commands/journal.ts]

Push to origin main is best-effort: when injected spawnFn returns non-zero on push the command prints an error but preserves the local commit and exits 0. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts with an injected spawnFn returning non-zero on push]

On success the command prints `CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED=<cycleId> sha=<sha>` as a parseable last line. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts asserting the stdout last line matches /^CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED=.+ sha=.+$/]
The `journal append` subcommand is wired into index.ts dispatch (reads stdin JSON, calls the command, returns its exit code). [oracle: file-assert grep -q "case 'journal'" index.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New code under src/commands/journal.ts; unit test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts; real-git integration test test/integration/journal-append-on-main.test.ts; index.ts dispatch (mirror the `case 'issue'` -> dispatchIssue --file-local path at index.ts:994-1035, which reads Bun.stdin.text(), JSON.parse, calls the on-main writer, prints a hint, returns exit code). REUSE the commit-tree-to-main plumbing: src/commands/issue-file.ts createLocalIssueOnMain and src/commands/issue-specify.ts specifyIssueOnMain are the templates (widened SpawnFn `{encoding:'utf8'; env?:Record<string,string>; input?:string}`, buildIndexEnv, checkMainUpToDate guard, commitOnMain vs commitTreeToMain, pushMainBestEffort). Factor shared helpers only if it stays surgical; do NOT reinvent the plumbing. Read journal.md from main via `git show main:scripts/cam/journal.md` (patterns.md US-006 CAM-86, line 77), never the working tree. Append after the existing tail, preserving the `<!-- ENTRIES_BELOW -->` marker and the existing entries (canonical format documented in scripts/cam/journal.md `## Format`). Determinism: started/closed come from the input JSON, clock is injected (mirror ship-finalize/specify, patterns.md gotcha); never Date.now()/new Date() for content. The header title em-dash (U+2014) is intentional and structural (all 33 existing entries use it); this story renders it in the title. Real-git integration test pattern: test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts is the exact template (gitAvailable skip guard via spawnSync git --version, mkdtempSync repo, git init + symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main + user config, seed+commit baseline journal.md on main, realSpawnFn forwarding env+input over spawnSync, afterEach rmSync cleanup) (patterns.md US-004 CAM-72, line 44). spawnSync does NOT throw on non-zero exit: check `(result.status ?? 1) !== 0` (patterns.md line 81). This command IS the gated write channel for the read-only orchestrator (the point of CAM-122); it replaces the ad-hoc jq-redirect / Write. Covers spec AC 1, 6, 7, 8.

userStories.title: Validation, optional fields, em-dash normalization, duplicate rejection
userStories.description: As a maintainer of the journal format, I need the command to validate required fields, render optional fields only when present, normalize em-dashes in the body, and reject a duplicate cycleId (with --force to replace in place), so that the journal stays well-formed and the format rule is owned by the command rather than by a fallible operator.
acceptanceCriteria: Required fields (cycleId, started, closed, branch, issue, outcome, summary) are validated: a missing required field exits non-zero with a clear error naming the missing field and appends nothing (no commit-tree call fires). [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts asserting exit non-zero, error text names the field, and the injected spawnFn recorded no commit-tree/update-ref call]

Optional fields (decisions, blockers, followups) render their bullet only when present; an absent optional produces no empty bullet in the rendered block. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts asserting the rendered body contains no `**Decisions**` bullet when decisions is absent and contains it when present]

An em-dash (U+2014) in any rendered body field is normalized away per the project no-em-dash rule, while the structural `## <cycleId> — <title>` header line retains its em-dash (consistent with the 33 existing entries). [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts asserting the rendered body contains no U+2014 and the title line still contains U+2014]

A duplicate cycleId (a `## <cycleId> ` header already present in journal.md) is rejected with a clear error and no append; the --force flag replaces the existing entry for that cycleId in place instead of appending. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts covering both the rejection (exit non-zero, no commit) and the --force in-place replacement (entry count unchanged, body updated)]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Extends src/commands/journal.ts (rendering + validation pure helpers) and test/commands/journal-append.test.ts. Validation guard order mirrors patterns.md US-003 CAM-107 (line 130): validate pure inputs BEFORE the `git show main:scripts/cam/journal.md` read where possible; duplicate-cycleId is a state check against the journal read from main. Discriminated-union error shape: members without `errors` must NOT carry it; callers narrow with `'errors' in result` (patterns.md line 130). Em-dash rule: normalize U+2014 ONLY in the body (Summary/Decisions/Blockers/Followups/Outcome text), NEVER the title (spec gotcha 4: deliberate exception specific to the journal title format, all 33 existing entries use it). Use the same normalization the project applies elsewhere for persisted .md (replace U+2014 with a project-approved substitute per ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md no-em-dash rule; the title is the documented exception). --force replace-in-place: locate the existing `## <cycleId> ` block in the journal text and swap it; do not duplicate. Determinism preserved (no Date.now/new Date). Covers spec AC 2, 3, 4, 5.
